scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: a bare except hides the real bug
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We misspelled total. That is a name error. But the bare except catches it, and prints, please enter a number. A misleading message, and the real bug is hidden. Never use except with no type. Catch the specific error you expect, such as value error, and let other errors show themselves.

props.why: A bare except catches every error, including your own typos, so it hides the real cause and shows a misleading message; catch specific types.

shorts.title: try and except
shorts.hook: "Put risky code in a try block."
shorts.script: Put risky code in a try block. If an error happens, Python jumps to a matching except block instead of stopping. Try, int of abc, except value error, print not a number. Now the program survives. Think of a safety net under a trapeze. The artist might fall, but the show goes on. Use it for input, files, and anything unpredictable. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: A safety net.

shorts.title: Catch the right error
shorts.hook: "Name the error type in the except line."
shorts.script: Name the error type in the except line. Except value error catches only value errors. Other errors still stop the program, and show their traceback, which is what you want. A traceback tells you what went wrong. Catch only the errors you expect, and know how to handle. Let the surprises show themselves, so you can fix them. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Be specific.

shorts.title: Else and finally
shorts.script: Two helpers complete the pattern. Else runs only when the try block finished without an error. Finally runs every time, error or not. Use it for cleanup, like closing a file. The order is try, except, else, finally. Together they let you describe every outcome clearly, and make sure the important cleanup is never skipped. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Four parts.

shorts.title: The bare except trap
shorts.script: A dangerous habit. You write except with no type. It catches every error, including your own typos. You misspell a name. Your program says, please enter a number. That message has nothing to do with the real problem. Always name the error type. Let the unexpected errors show themselves, so that you can find and fix the real bug. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Always name the type.

shorts.hook: "Why did the exception go to therapy?"
shorts.script: Why did the exception go to therapy? It could not handle it. Your challenge. Ask the user for a number with input. Convert it with int, inside a try block. If the conversion fails, print not a number, instead of crashing. Test it with the word abc, and with the number twelve. Share your code in the comments below. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
